mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financial conditions compressing near-term discounting of equity cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns during Fed rate hikes are not statistically different from a 0.0% baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market tightening reduces recession risk and boosts investor confidence.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.5 percentage points for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such labor market tightening regimes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a 0.0% baseline (t-test p > 0.05 over 5 such regimes).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds INDPRO by more than 2% for three consecutive months, it indicates robust demand growth that precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: During such gaps, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in at least 4 out of 5 occurrences.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 3% for two consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which is associated with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investor risk aversion rises.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In supply contraction regimes, 5-day forward returns are not consistently negative (median < 0 but not statistically significant at p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL prints a monthly YoY increase above 3% in a month following a Fed pause, it predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to market anticipation of future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY % change > 3% and previous month FEDFUNDS < 5.0%
failure_condition: During such events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly PAYEMS reading above 160,000 for three consecutive months suggests labor market expansion, which is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return via optimism about economic strength.
failure_condition: In such labor expansions, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than a 0.0% baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST (housing starts) of at least 5% and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 2% jointly predict a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as a dual demand signal emerges.
candidate_trigger: HOUST up > 5% AND RSAFS up > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: During such dual upturns, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in FEDFUNDS below 4.00% for four consecutive months in a non-recessionary macro regime is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower policy rates encourage equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4.00% for four consecutive months and GDP growth > 1% in prior quarter
failure_condition: In such regimes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than a 0.0% baseline (p > 0.05).
